title: Apalachicola's local state of emergency extended - NewsBreak
text: APALACHICOLA, Fla. (WMBB) – Franklin County commissioners extended the local state emergency over Apalachicola’s water quality. The water problems began years ago but got worse after Hurricane Helene last September. The aerator was damaged and won’t be replace until later in July. Prior to the state of emergency people complained the water smelled and tasted bad. The city has been flushing the water distribution to remove any remaining odors. And the precautionary boil water notice has been lifted. It’s improved somewhat, but many still say they won’t drink it. In the meantime, the city has been offering water, ice, laundry, and shower facilities for residents. Taylor County sent 18 pallets of water. “I do want to thank, sincerely thank Commissioner Newman because he’s from Taylor County, that’s been one of the worst hit counties in the previous year with hurricanes,” said County Commissioner Jessica Ward. “And yet there he is extending a helping hand. And I guess he got this contact. It’s blue arctic water. Every they’re from down south. They came from Dade City, made a five-hour trip to deliver water.” The Franklin County Commission is sending a letter of appreciation to the Taylor County Board of County Commissioners to thank them for their help. The state of emergency would have expired this Friday evening, July 18th at 6:15 p.m, but today’s vote will extend it further. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to mypanhandle.com.
